text:
The Rangers visit Columbus tonight (NYR 3.08 expected goals, CBJ 2.98) in a matchup the numbers see as nearly even. At five on five, NYR has taken 50% of the expected goals and CBJ 53%. The Blue Jackets have allowed more chances (3.21 expected goals against per 60, versus 2.83 for NYR), and both teams have been giving up goals at different rates: CBJ at 4.2 a game, NYR at 2.33. Special teams lean toward New York. The Rangers' power play generates 0.74 expected goals a game to Columbus's 0.45, though NYR takes 4.4 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays. CBJ's penalty kill has allowed 0.76 expected goals a game against 0.43 for NYR's.

In net, projected starters Dylan Garand (NYR) and Jet Greaves (CBJ) arrive in opposite shapes. Garand is at +0.55 goals saved above expected this season with a .915 save percentage, while Greaves sits at -1.54 with a .874. Last year Greaves was at +15.02 over 55 games, and Garand was +3.88 over three. Garand is in the picture because Igor Shesterkin is on injured reserve, which the model already counts. Greaves has the track record to bounce back.

Form is mixed. NYR is 3-2-0 over its last five with 52% of the expected goals, though it was routed 7-1 at New Jersey on Thursday. CBJ is 2-3-0 with 47%, and lost 7-3 to Florida last time out. Alexis Lafrenière (32% to score, 59% for a point) rides a six-game point streak, and Mika Zibanejad, atop the power play, is the likeliest Ranger to post two points (26%). For Columbus, Adam Fantilli (26% to score) and Matthew Knies (25%) lead the power play.
